subject: Re: Uptime math — partial cache-path degradation & maintenance overlap
messages:
From: Mike Chen <ops-support@acme-corp.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Discrepancy in Nov 12-13 availability numbers — request for apportionment

Hi Aditya / Marissa,

We reviewed the uptime report you sent for the Nov 12–13 window and we're seeing a much larger hit on our side than the numbers in the ledger. From our telemetry (sample attached) we observed a sustained 8–15% error-rate on calls routed via the US-West cache path and a p95 latency uplift of ~220ms for requests that hit cold cache situations.

EdgeFlow (our CDN) also sent a planned maintenance notice that coincides with part of the window; they claim it only affected 2/6 US POPs. Given that, we're asking Redwood to rerun the availability calculation with an apportionment that:
- excludes the periods where EdgeFlow confirms maintenance on their POPs;
- attributes only the fraction of traffic routed to the affected POPs toward the credit calculation (i.e., do not treat the whole account as degraded).

Attached: acme_http_sample_log_20261112.csv (sample request traces). Please confirm what you need from us to make this request actionable.

Thanks,
Mike Chen
Ops Support
Acme Commerce

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chen <ops-support@acme-corp.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 12:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in Nov 12-13 availability numbers — request for apportionment

Mike — thanks for the data and the heads-up. We got the CSV and initial samples look helpful.

Quick notes:
- Contractually, our SLA defines availability at the account level, but there is an apportionment clause that allows excluding third-party maintenance windows where the root cause is demonstrated to be outside Redwood's control.
- To make a clean apportionment we need: (a) EdgeFlow's maintenance ticket/timestamps, (b) a mapping of your request-to-POP distribution during the window (or a representative sample), and (c) the probe ids/redwood-pop mapping for the affected times.

Marissa — tagging you for the telemetry alignment (I think we saw increased 5xxs on the US-W gateway metrics for those timestamps). Kimberly, please pull the pop-level request distribution for Nov 12 02:00–08:00 UTC and Nov 13 01:00–06:00 UTC.

Proposed approach (temporary, to get consensus):
1) Identify the exact maintenance window(s) from EdgeFlow.
2) Partition the request stream by POP; for the portion served by affected POPs, count degradations per usual SLO rules.
3) For the remainder of traffic, keep the ledger as-is.
4) Compute a prorated credit = account_impact_fraction * standard_credit_amount; deliver as a one-time billing credit.

If EdgeFlow confirms full responsibility and it only touched a subset of POPs, that seems like a fair apportionment. We'll try to have a draft calculation and spreadsheet for you by EOD Friday.

- Aditya Rao
Sr. Account Lead | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Mike Chen <ops-support@acme-corp.com>, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in Nov 12-13 availability numbers — request for apportionment

Hi Mike,

I pulled the raw telemetry and ran a quick pop-level breakdown. Findings (high level):
- Between 2026-11-12T02:12:00Z and 2026-11-12T05:45:00Z the affected US-West POPs saw an increase in 5xx rate from baseline 0.4% -> 12.7%.
- Median p95 latency for cache-miss routes jumped from ~85ms -> 305ms in the same window.
- Traffic routing logs show ~27% of your account's requests were routed through the affected POPs during peak. That matches the sample you attached.

If we treat the event as a partial-path degradation (not a full account outage) we can compute an apportionment credit using a two-step formula:
A) impact_share = (requests_through_affected_pops) / (total_account_requests)
B) effective_degrade_fraction = impact_share * (degrade_severity_factor)
Where degrade_severity_factor is derived from how many requests exceeded the SLO thresholds (we measured ~9% of total requests in the affected POPs as SLO breachers).

Applied to your window this yields an effective_degrade_fraction ~ 0.27 * 0.09 = 0.0243 (2.43% account-level impact).
For monthly SLA crediting that would translate to X hours of credit; I attached a draft spreadsheet showing the mapping to our standard credit tiers.

Two operational caveats:
1) If EdgeFlow's maintenance shows a notice that was an RCA of a Redwood-dependent routing change, we cannot exclude it.
2) We need a signed acceptance from Acme on the apportionment method before we finalize a billing credit.

Attached: apportionment_spreadsheet_20261124.xlsx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discrepancy in Nov 12-13 availability numbers — request for apportionment

Aditya/Marissa,

Confirming EdgeFlow performed a rolling config change to a cache-invalidator during 2026-11-12T02:00:00Z -> 2026-11-12T04:30:00Z. We impacted two of six US-W POPs; the maintenance notice (edgeflow_maint_notice_20261112.pdf) was distributed in advance to customers. The ticket ID for the change is EF-48921: https://edgeflow.status/EF-48921 (internal public uptime page).

We measured higher revalidation rates and a transient control-plane race causing elevated 5xxs on the two POPs. That said, we do not have visibility into your origin or Redwood routing decisions — only that our systems served a subset of your traffic and we acknowledge responsibility for the work.

Happy to provide any raw logs or a CID-to-POP mapping if that helps expedite the apportionment calculation.

Regards,
Miguel Santos
SRE Lead | EdgeFlow
miguel@edgeflow.io

Mike — following up with the formal calculation and next steps.

Summary:
- EdgeFlow has confirmed a maintenance window that corresponds to part of the degraded window and that it affected 2/6 US-W POPs (ticket EF-48921).
- Redwood telemetry shows ~27% of your account's requests hit affected POPs in the window and ~9% of those requests breached SLOs.
- Using the formula Marissa outlined, the computed account-level impact is ~2.43%.

Proposal:
1) We will issue a one-time credit equal to 2.43% of the affected billing period charges, applied to your Dec invoice.
2) Before applying the credit we need Acme to sign an acknowledgement of the apportionment method and the supporting artifacts (EdgeFlow ticket + Redwood pop mapping). I'll attach the short confirmation template.
3) If you disagree with the numbers we can open a joint replay session (EdgeFlow + Acme + Redwood) to walk the traces — but that will delay crediting.

If you accept this path, reply with: "ACCEPT APPORTIONMENT METHOD" and we will queue the credit. If you want the joint replay, propose 2x 60-minute slots next week.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Sr. Account Lead | Redwood Inference
